questions.q: Shenton's line is drawn from:
opts: The superior margin of the pubic ramus to the head
The inferior margin of the superior pubic ramus (laterally) to the medial part of head and neck
The greater trochanter to the lesser trochanter
The iliac crest to the ischial tuberosity
questions.exp: Shenton's line: inferior margin of superior pubic ramus (laterally) -> medial part of head and neck. (Book p160)

questions.q: Pathology in the hip causes disturbance in:
questions.exp: Pathology causes disturbance in Shenton's line. (Book p160)

questions.q: The normal neck-shaft angle in adults is:
questions.exp: Neck-shaft angle: normal is 130-135 degree (adults). (Book p160)

questions.q: An increased neck-shaft angle is called:
questions.exp: Up neck-shaft angle: coxa valga. (Book p160)

questions.q: A decreased neck-shaft angle is called:
questions.exp: Down neck-shaft angle: coxa vara. (Book p160)

questions.q: The proximal femur in children has a growth plate; the capital femoral epiphysis is the:
questions.exp: Proximal femur in children has a growth plate; capital femoral epiphysis: head of the femur epiphysis. (Book p160)

questions.q: The pathogenesis of coxa vara is:
opts: Injury to the growth plate of head of femur - greater trochanter continues to grow while head and neck stop growing
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head only
questions.exp: Injury to the growth plate of head of femur -> greater trochanter continues to grow, head and neck stop growing -> coxa vara. (Book p160)

questions.q: In coxa vara, the structure that continues to grow is the:
questions.exp: Greater trochanter continues to grow; head and neck stop growing. (Book p160)

questions.q: The types of coxa vara are:
questions.exp: Types of coxa vara: infantile/primary and acquired/secondary. (Book p160)

questions.q: Acquired/secondary coxa vara is seen in:
questions.exp: Acquired/secondary coxa vara: Perthes disease, SCFE. (Book p160)

questions.q: Trendelenburg gait in coxa vara is due to:
questions.exp: Trendelenburg gait: failure of hip abduction. (Book p160)

questions.q: Obligate external rotation in coxa vara is:
opts: External rotation of the hip (knee goes out) on flexion of hip
External rotation on hip extension only
questions.exp: Obligate external rotation: external rotation of hip (knee goes out) on flexion of hip. (Book p160)

questions.q: In coxa vara there is limitation of:
questions.exp: Limitation of abduction and internal rotation. (Book p160)

questions.q: Another clinical feature of coxa vara is:
questions.exp: Clinical feature: limb shortening. (Book p160)

questions.q: The etiology of congenital coxa vara is:
questions.exp: Etiology: damage to Fairbank's triangle. (Book p161)

questions.q: Fairbank's triangle is a part of the:
questions.exp: Fairbank's triangle: part of neck of femur. (Book p161)

questions.q: As per the note, the triangle seen in TB (hip) is:
questions.exp: Note: Babcock's triangle is seen in TB. (Book p161)

questions.q: The SCFE mnemonic is:
opts: Neck stays inside the acetabulum while head slips
Head remains inside the acetabulum whereas neck slips
questions.exp: SCFE mnemonic: head remains inside the acetabulum whereas neck slips. (Book p161)

questions.q: The pathogenesis of SCFE is:
opts: Fracture of the growth plate (Type I Salter-Harris) - head and neck are disrupted
questions.exp: Pathogenesis: fracture of the growth plate (Type I Salter-Harris); head and neck are disrupted; head remains in the acetabulum and neck slips. (Book p161)

questions.q: SCFE is a Type I Salter-Harris injury because:
opts: The fracture line goes through all layers
It is a fracture of the growth plate without injuring the germinal layer
questions.exp: SCFE: fracture of the growth plate (Type I Salter-Harris). (Book p161)

questions.q: The m/c cause of SCFE is:
questions.exp: Etiology: idiopathic: m/c cause. (Book p161)

questions.q: SCFE is associated with endocrinopathy d/t:
questions.exp: Associated with endocrinopathy (d/t sex hormone imbalance in puberty). (Book p161)

questions.q: The m/c endocrinopathies associated with SCFE are:
questions.exp: M/c: hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, increased GH. (Book p161)

questions.q: SCFE is more common in:
questions.exp: General features: male > female. (Book p161)

questions.q: The risk factor for SCFE in children is:
questions.exp: Risk factor: more weight for age in children. (Book p161)

questions.q: In SCFE, the proportion of bilateral cases is:
questions.exp: 40% cases are bilateral (60% cases if associated with endocrinopathy). (Book p161)

questions.q: SCFE presents at puberty at the age of:
questions.exp: Presents at puberty: males 13-17 yrs, females 11-14 yrs. (Book p161)

questions.q: In a SCFE patient with endocrinopathy, features may include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Endocrinopathy features: hypogonadism, voice change, gynecomastia. (Book p161)

questions.q: Clinically, SCFE shows:
questions.exp: Clinical features include coxa vara features. (Book p161)

questions.q: Trethowan's sign on X-ray in SCFE is:
opts: Line drawn on the lateral aspect of neck of femur does not intersect with the head of femur
Absent Trethowan's line intersecting the head
questions.exp: Trethowan's sign: line drawn on the lateral aspect of neck of femur does not intersect with the head of femur. (Book p161)

questions.q: Treatment of SCFE is:
opts: Closed reduction + internal fixation + in situ pinning
questions.exp: Treatment: closed reduction + internal fixation + in situ pinning. (Book p161)

questions.q: Osteochondrosis is:
opts: A self-limiting abnormality of bone growth
questions.exp: Osteochondrosis is a self-limiting abnormality of bone growth. (Book p162)

questions.q: Osteochondrosis involves:
opts: The centres of ossification in the epiphysis
questions.exp: Involves centres of ossification in the epiphysis. (Book p162)

questions.q: Osteochondrosis begins in childhood as a necrotic condition, d/t:
opts: Primary vascular event or repetitive trauma
questions.exp: Begins in childhood as a necrotic condition; d/t primary vascular event or repetitive trauma. (Book p162)

questions.q: The m/c osteochondrosis is Perthes disease, which involves the:
questions.exp: Osteochondritis - bone table: Perthes disease (m/c): femoral epiphysis. (Book p162)

questions.q: Kohler's disease involves the:
questions.exp: Kohler's disease: navicular bone. (Book p162)

questions.q: Freiberg's disease involves the:
questions.exp: Freiberg's disease: lunate. (Book p162)

questions.q: Panner's disease involves the:
questions.exp: Panner's disease: capitulum (elbow pain). (Book p162)

questions.q: Osgood-Schlatter's disease involves the:
questions.exp: Osgood-Schlatter's disease: tibial tuberosity. (Book p162)

questions.q: Sever's disease involves the:
questions.exp: Sever's disease: calcaneal epiphysis. (Book p162)

questions.q: Perthes disease is also known as:
questions.exp: Perthes disease: aka coxa plana / Legg-Calve-Perthes disease. (Book p162)

questions.q: Perthes disease is:
opts: Idiopathic, spontaneous osteonecrosis (Chandler's disease in adults)
questions.exp: Perthes: idiopathic, spontaneous osteonecrosis (Chandler's disease in adults). (Book p162)

questions.q: The foveolar flow is the predominant source of blood supply for the head of femur at age:
questions.exp: Source of blood supply for head of femur: foveolar flow: predominant source at age <4 yrs. (Book p162)
